title: Thread
description: The free-ranging, UNSCOPED conversation surface — the only conversation surface in the product (product-flows.md §Threads, tables & outputs). A thread ROAMS: it carries no fixed Dataset; the agent resolves each message's own scope (decisions/0004-scope-binds-to-table-not-thread.md). It persists (recency-ordered by updated_at, searchable, deletable) and does NOT fork. Persisted at var/threads/<id>/thread.json. Each user message is passed to the agent without backend regex/phrase-list pre-routing; it may also carry request attachments for a pinned Dataset/template context. The Answer branch carries the real natural-language answer on the agent message's `content` plus its inline `resolution.citations` when it relies on database values (whole-DB, permission-bounded, fail-closed at the registered read-only hospital DB). If the agent calls `ask_user_question`, the agent message carries `resolution.ask_user_questions` until the composer submits or skips the answers.

title.description: Derived from the first user message (trimmed to ~60 chars); "New thread" if none yet.

updated_at.description: ISO-8601 (UTC) last-activity time. Drives recency ordering in the Threads list.

status.description: Operational lifecycle for the latest agent turn. `running` while a streaming answer is still in progress; `complete` once the agent has answered, asked follow-up questions, spawned a table, failed gracefully, or the thread has no in-flight turn. Optional for older thread files; readers treat absent as `complete`.

messages.description: The conversation, in order. A user message is followed by the agent message carrying its routing resolution.

artifact_ids.description: Back-references to first-class tables this thread spawned (table metadata lives as `tables` rows in var/state.db per Q36; a thread only references them for inline inspectors). Empty [] in this issue; Issue 2 appends.

id.description: Stable message id, minted as `msg-<uuid4 hex prefix>`.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 (UTC) time the message was appended.

attachments.description: Library items the user pinned to this request. At most one Dataset and one template; a Dataset pins this message's answer scope, and a template gives the agent explicit template context.

type.description: The library item kind pinned to the request.

id.description: The Dataset id or template id.

resolution.description: The agent result metadata, present on an AGENT message that answers a user request or asks structured follow-up questions.

output.description: table -> the output is a populated Table (the spawn is owned in tables); chat -> the output is an Answer: natural-language text in `content`, with `citations` when it relies on database values.

artifact_id.description: Set when a table is spawned; null for a chat output.

seam.description: Reserved for a not-yet-built output. Null for both a Table output and an Answer output.

citations.description: For an Answer: the inline sources backing database-derived values in `content`, one per `[1]`/`[2]` marker. A source citation re-extracts the cited value next to its identity; an aggregate citation also carries denominator/completeness and covered rows. Absent/empty for a table output.

activity.description: For a streaming Answer: bounded live activity forwarded from the agent session (tool calls / thinking), rendered inline while the answer is streaming.

ask_user_questions.description: Present when the agent called the generic ask_user_question tool and the composer must collect answers before the agent can continue.

patch.description: Opaque resource-specific proposal payload. The thread contract intentionally does not define the Dataset or Template patch grammar yet; the write tool that consumes the approved proposal owns validation.

citation.description: One inline source behind an Answer — the evidence source object plus its `[n]` marker. Surfaced as a clickable citation that opens the evidence panel. Aggregate citations additionally open the aggregate query, denominator/completeness, and covered rows.

kind.description: source -> direct/source-row evidence; aggregate -> aggregate claim with denominator/completeness and covered rows. Omitted legacy values are treated as source by readers.

marker.description: The numeric inline marker in the answer, e.g. "1" for `[1]`.

database.description: The registered clinical database slug the value was read from.

query.description: The SELECT that re-extracts the cited value beside its identity (a chat read: read-only, no cohort injection).

explanation.description: What the value is / how it was computed.

row_id.description: For a free-text source (a note/comment): the cited record's primary key. Free-text only.

row_key.description: For a free-text source: the column the primary key is in. Free-text only.

citations.description: For a free-text source: the verbatim substring(s) of the record that state the value (never a paraphrase).

denominator.description: Aggregate citations only: denominator metadata shown in the evidence panel.

completeness.description: Aggregate citations only: completeness metadata, e.g. recorded/eligible rows.

covered_rows.description: Aggregate citations only: source citations for the rows behind the aggregate, drillable from the evidence panel.

scope.description: The slice this message's answer was computed at, plus a clinician-readable disclosure. A thread is unscoped; each message may answer within a named Dataset or across the whole hospital database.

kind.description: whole_db -> the whole hospital database; dataset -> a named Dataset.

dataset_id.description: The Dataset id for a `dataset` scope; null for `whole_db`.

disclosure.description: Clinician-readable one-liner, e.g. "answered across the whole hospital database".
